papers.title_zh: 三级护理中心急性呼吸道病毒感染儿科患者的呼吸道病毒负担和医疗保健利用情况。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory viral infections, particularly Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and influenza, are major causes of pediatric morbidity, hospitalization, and healthcare strain during winter seasons. This study aims to evaluate the clinical and epidemiological burden of RSV and influenza in pediatric patients and assess associated healthcare resource utilization. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 1428 patients of all ages, including a pediatric subgroup (0–14 years) who presented to an emergency department in a tertiary care center in Saudi Arabia between October 2024 and March 2025. Viral pathogens were detected using a rapid antigen test detecting SARS‐CoV‐2, influenza A/B, RSV, and adenovirus. Descriptive epidemiological analysis was performed to assess clinical trends and healthcare utilization. Results A total of 1428 patients were tested, of whom 257 (18%) confirmed positive for respiratory viruses. The pediatric group ( n = 158) had a mean age of 3.2 years and was largely composed of young children, with 48% under 2 years and 76% under 5. RSV (37%) and Influenza A (36%) predominated, followed by Influenza B (14%), SARS‐CoV‐2 (7.0%), and Adenovirus (5.1%). Peak positivity occurred in January (34% of detected cases) with continued detections into March (15%). Most children (60%) were discharged, while 31% required hospitalization; ICU admissions were infrequent. Oxygen therapy was required in 12% ( n = 19), and antiviral therapy (oseltamivir) was administered in 7 patients. Advanced respiratory support included high‐flow nasal cannula (HFNC; n = 11) and non‐invasive ventilation (continuous positive airway pressure [CPAP] and bilevel positive airway pressure [BiPAP]; n = 12), highlighting substantial healthcare demands. Conclusion This study shows a substantial winter burden from RSV and influenza in young children, leading to high emergency visits, admissions, and respiratory support use. Increased medication demand highlights the need for proactive planning, resource allocation, and preventive strategies to manage seasonal healthcare pressures effectively.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒感染,特别是 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和流感,是冬季儿科发病、住院和医疗压力的主要原因。本研究旨在评估儿科患者 RSV 和流感的临床和流行病学负担,并评估相关的医疗资源利用率。方法 这项回顾性 队列研究 研究分析了 1428 名各个年龄段的患者,包括 2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 3 月期间到沙特阿拉伯三级护理中心急诊科就诊的儿科亚组(0-14 岁)。使用快速抗原测试检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感、RSV 和腺病毒,检测病毒病原体。进行描述性流行病学分析以评估临床趋势和医疗保健利用。结果 共有 1428 名患者接受了检测,其中 257 名患者(18%)确诊呼吸道病毒阳性。儿科组 (n = 158) 的平均年龄为 3.2 岁,主要由幼儿组成,其中 48% 为 2 岁以下,76% 为 5 岁以下。以 RSV (37%) 和甲型流感 (36%) 为主,其次是乙型流感 (14%)、SARS-CoV-2 (7.0%) 和腺病毒 (5.1%)。阳性率高峰出现在 1 月份(检测到的病例的 34%),并持续检测到 3 月份(15%)。大多数儿童(60%)已出院,31% 需要住院治疗;入住 ICU 的情况并不常见。12%(n = 19)需要氧疗,7 名患者接受了 抗病毒药物 治疗(奥司他韦)。高级呼吸支持包括高流量鼻插管 (HFNC;n = 11) 和无创通气(持续气道正压通气 [CPAP] 和双水平气道正压通气 [BiPAP];n = 12),凸显了巨大的医疗保健需求。结论 这项研究表明,冬季 RSV 和流感对幼儿造成了巨大的负担,导致急诊就诊、入院和呼吸支持使用率较高。药物需求的增加凸显了主动规划、资源分配和预防策略的必要性,以有效管理季节性医疗压力。

papers.title: Integrated Hospital, Emergency Department, and Community Surveillance for Respiratory Viruses in Milan, Italy.
papers.abstract: Respiratory virus circulation may vary across healthcare settings and age groups, potentially limiting the interpretability of surveillance based on a single source. In Milan, Italy, established community- and emergency department-based systems coexist with hospital laboratory testing, but hospital ward-level data are not routinely integrated. The aims of this study were to describe respiratory viruses' epidemiology and assess whether ward-based surveillance complements community and ED surveillance. We analyzed molecular test results from respiratory samples collected from January 1, 2024 (W1/2024) to October 12, 2025 (W41/2025) in community, ED, and hospital ward settings. Viruses included influenza A (IAV), influenza B (IBV), RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 (with extended panels in a subset). Among 8029 samples, overall positivity for ≥ 1 virus was 46.8%, highest in ED (51.1%) and community (50.5%) and lower in wards (36.7%) (p < 0.001). During 2024-2025, IAV was first detected in wards (W33/2024) and peaked earlier in wards (W2/2025) than community (W3/2025) and ED (W4/2025). IBV was first detected in ED (W36/2024) and peaked in ED (W5/2025), community (W7/2025), and wards (W8/2025). RSV reappeared first in community (W37/2024) and peaked in community/ED (W50/2024) and later in wards (W2/2025). Respiratory virus positivity and descriptive peak timing differed across healthcare settings and age groups. Ward-based surveillance provided complementary information for hospitalized and older populations, but it was not consistently earlier or superior to community or ED surveillance. Integrated, multi-setting surveillance can improve situational awareness when interpreted alongside differences in tested populations, testing indications, and clinical outcome availability.

papers.title_zh: 意大利米兰的呼吸道病毒综合医院、急诊科和社区 监测。
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory virus circulation may vary across healthcare settings and age groups, potentially limiting the interpretability of surveillance based on a single source. In Milan, Italy, established community- and emergency department-based systems coexist with hospital laboratory testing, but hospital ward-level data are not routinely integrated. The aims of this study were to describe respiratory viruses' epidemiology and assess whether ward-based surveillance complements community and ED surveillance. We analyzed molecular test results from respiratory samples collected from January 1, 2024 (W1/2024) to October 12, 2025 (W41/2025) in community, ED, and hospital ward settings. Viruses included influenza A (IAV), influenza B (IBV), RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 (with extended panels in a subset). Among 8029 samples, overall positivity for ≥ 1 virus was 46.8%, highest in ED (51.1%) and community (50.5%) and lower in wards (36.7%) (p < 0.001). During 2024-2025, IAV was first detected in wards (W33/2024) and peaked earlier in wards (W2/2025) than community (W3/2025) and ED (W4/2025). IBV was first detected in ED (W36/2024) and peaked in ED (W5/2025), community (W7/2025), and wards (W8/2025). RSV reappeared first in community (W37/2024) and peaked in community/ED (W50/2024) and later in wards (W2/2025). Respiratory virus positivity and descriptive peak timing differed across healthcare settings and age groups. Ward-based surveillance provided complementary information for hospitalized and older populations, but it was not consistently earlier or superior to community or ED surveillance. Integrated, multi-setting surveillance can improve situational awareness when interpreted alongside differences in tested populations, testing indications, and clinical outcome availability.

papers.title: RSVPreF3OA vaccine responses in kidney transplant recipients and dialysis patients versus healthy controls.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory illness in vulnerable populations, including kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) and dialysis patients (DPs). Despite the availability of RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccines, immune phenotyping of vaccine-specific B and T cells in KTRs and DPs remains limited. We hypothesized that RSVPreF3OA vaccination induces distinct immune signatures in KTRs and DPs compared with healthy controls (HCs), reflecting the impact of immunosuppression and uraemia on vaccine-induced B and T cell responses. METHODS: In this observational cohort, we analysed humoral and cellular responses following routine vaccination with the adjuvanted prefusion F protein-based RSVPreF3OA vaccine in 23 KTRs, 14 DPs and 24 HCs. Blood and saliva were collected at baseline and on days 30 and 90 post-vaccination. RSV-specific serum immunoglobulin G/immunoglobulin A, salivary antibodies and antigen-specific B and T cells were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and spectral flow cytometry, with tetanus- and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2-specific responses assessed in parallel. RESULTS: In KTRs, vaccination induced increases in serum and salivary antibodies, expansion of RSV-specific B cells with enrichment of a switched memory phenotype unique to RSV-specific B cells and induction of RSV-A- and RSV-B-specific T cells with effector cytokine production. These signatures resembled those observed in HCs, whereas responses in DPs were delayed and attenuated. Across cohorts, RSV-specific B and T cells showed comparable phenotypic and functional characteristics. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides detailed immunophenotyping of RSVPreF3OA vaccine responses in KTRs, DPs and HCs over 90 days, showing that RSVPreF3OA vaccination induces protective RSV responses among KTRs comparable to HCs while DPs mount modestly lower cellular and humoral responses.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory illness in vulnerable populations, including kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) and dialysis patients (DPs). Despite the availability of RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccines, immune phenotyping of vaccine-specific B and T cells in KTRs and DPs remains limited.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: In this observational cohort, we analysed humoral and cellular responses following routine vaccination with the adjuvanted prefusion F protein-based RSVPreF3OA vaccine in 23 KTRs, 14 DPs and 24 healthy controls (HCs).
analysis_en.methods: Blood and saliva were collected at baseline and on days 30 and 90 post-vaccination. RSV-specific serum immunoglobulin G/immunoglobulin A, salivary antibodies and antigen-specific B and T cells were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and spectral flow cytometry, with tetanus- and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2-specific responses assessed in parallel.
analysis_en.main_results: In KTRs, vaccination induced increases in serum and salivary antibodies, expansion of RSV-specific B cells with enrichment of a switched memory phenotype unique to RSV-specific B cells and induction of RSV-A- and RSV-B-specific T cells with effector cytokine production. These signatures resembled those observed in HCs, whereas responses in DPs were delayed and attenuated. Across cohorts, RSV-specific B and T cells showed comparable phenotypic and functional characteristics.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: This study provides detailed immunophenotyping of RSVPreF3OA vaccine responses in KTRs, DPs and HCs over 90 days, showing that RSVPreF3OA vaccination induces protective RSV responses among KTRs comparable to HCs while DPs mount modestly lower cellular and humoral responses.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that RSVPreF3OA vaccination may be effective in KTRs, supporting its use in this vulnerable population, while DPs may require additional strategies to enhance vaccine responses.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational with a small sample size, limiting generalisability. However, the detailed immunophenotyping provides strong evidence for differential vaccine responses across cohorts.

papers.title_zh: 肾移植受者和透析患者与健康对照者的 RSVPreF3OA 疫苗 反应。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory illness in vulnerable populations, including kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) and dialysis patients (DPs). Despite the availability of RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccines, immune phenotyping of vaccine-specific B and T cells in KTRs and DPs remains limited. We hypothesized that RSVPreF3OA vaccination induces distinct immune signatures in KTRs and DPs compared with healthy controls (HCs), reflecting the impact of immunosuppression and uraemia on vaccine-induced B and T cell responses. METHODS: In this observational cohort, we analysed humoral and cellular responses following routine vaccination with the adjuvanted prefusion F protein-based RSVPreF3OA vaccine in 23 KTRs, 14 DPs and 24 HCs. Blood and saliva were collected at baseline and on days 30 and 90 post-vaccination. RSV-specific serum immunoglobulin G/immunoglobulin A, salivary antibodies and antigen-specific B and T cells were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and spectral flow cytometry, with tetanus- and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2-specific responses assessed in parallel. RESULTS: In KTRs, vaccination induced increases in serum and salivary antibodies, expansion of RSV-specific B cells with enrichment of a switched memory phenotype unique to RSV-specific B cells and induction of RSV-A- and RSV-B-specific T cells with effector cytokine production. These signatures resembled those observed in HCs, whereas responses in DPs were delayed and attenuated. Across cohorts, RSV-specific B and T cells showed comparable phenotypic and functional characteristics. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides detailed immunophenotyping of RSVPreF3OA vaccine responses in KTRs, DPs and HCs over 90 days, showing that RSVPreF3OA vaccination induces protective RSV responses among KTRs comparable to HCs while DPs mount modestly lower cellular and humoral responses.

papers.title: Unlocking the value of RSV vaccination in Japan: a return on investment analysis using an integrated actuarial-macroeconomic model
papers.abstract: Objective Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant morbidity and mortality among older adults and individuals with chronic conditions. This study conducted a cost–benefit analysis (CBA) to evaluate the societal value of RSV vaccination with the adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein (RSVPreF3) vaccine among older adults aged ≥60 years and high-risk adults aged 50–59 years in Japan. Methods An actuarial population projection model, combined with a full CBA framework adapted to the Japanese setting, was used to estimate costs and benefits of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination versus no vaccination over a 10-year time horizon. Deterministic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess parameter uncertainty. Results Our results indicate that a 5-year vaccination program among older adults, including those aged 50–59 years at higher risk for severe RSV disease and those aged ≥60 years, was associated with substantial economic benefits. Among older adults aged ≥60 years, the total return on investment (ROI) was 3.3 with or without deadweight loss (DWL), with vaccination projected to avert Japanese Yen (JPY) 35,501 M in productive output loss, save JPY 1,178,403 M in direct healthcare costs, and prevent JPY 10,699,729 M in monetized quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) loss. For high-risk adults aged 50–59 years, the total ROI was 3.7 without DWL and 3.8 with DWL, with corresponding reductions of JPY 17,889 M in productive output loss, JPY 10,400 M in healthcare costs, and JPY 266,116 M in monetized QALY loss. Conclusion Overall, adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination among older adults in Japan represents good value for money from a societal perspective, where vaccine acquisition and administration costs are expected to be outweighed by substantial health, productivity, and broader economic benefits.

papers.title: Regional, altitudinal, and age-specific heterogeneity of bronchiolitis hospitalization seasonality in Ecuador, 2007–2024, and implications for RSV immunoprophylaxis timing
papers.abstract: Background Acute bronchiolitis, mainly attributed to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), is the leading cause of infant hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease worldwide. Nirsevimab and maternal RSVpreF (Abrysvo) confer about 6 months of protection, so timing relative to the season affects their impact. Ecuador spans the equator from sea level to valleys above 4,000 m and is considering introducing these products, yet lacks subnational evidence on the seasonality of bronchiolitis, altitudinal patterning, or post-pandemic stability. Methods We conducted a national ecological time-series analysis of hospital discharges from the Ecuadorian Statistics Institute, 2007–2024 (19,788,097 discharges; 204 of 224 cantons had complete data and formed the analytic panel). The primary outcome was acute bronchiolitis (ICD-10 code J21) in children younger than 12 months ( n = 23,190 nationally; 22,724 in the panel), with secondary outcomes across three RSV-relevant age bands, ICD-10 code J21 under 5 years, and two RSV-specific ICD-10 codes (J12.1 and J20.5; 2018–2024). K35 (appendicitis) was a negative control. Analyses combined circular seasonality metrics with block-bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), year-by-year disaggregation, and complementary sensitivity analyses [Moving Epidemics Method (MEM), Bai–Perron breaks, and lagged climate correlations]. Results The weighted circular peak month of infant bronchiolitis hospitalizations shifted after the pandemic in Costa (+2.16 months), Sierra (+1.22), and Amazonía (+1.91), attenuating with altitude from +2.19 months below 500 m to +0.88 at 1,500–3,000 m. Costa was stable across 2022–2024; Sierra and, more so, Amazonía varied widely year to year (Amazonía peak ranged March–July, n = 37–42/year), so the pooled estimate should be read with caution. The composite RSV-coded outcome tracked ICD-10 code J21's timing closely in Costa (0.15-month difference) and Sierra (0.40), supporting ICD-10 code J21 as a reasonable RSV proxy in both, and the three regional peaks now span 2 months. Conclusion Bronchiolitis seasonality in Ecuador changed after the pandemic, most clearly and stably in Costa; Sierra showed a transient 2022 perturbation with partial reversion by 2023–2024, and Amazonía's estimates remained unstable and underpowered. As region-tailored estimates are less stable in Sierra and Amazonía than in Costa, a single national window (nirsevimab February–April; maternal RSVpreF for pregnancies expected to deliver January–May) is a more defensible starting point, pending confirmation from further seasons and, ideally, laboratory-confirmed surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of subnational evidence on bronchiolitis seasonality, altitudinal patterning, and post-pandemic stability in Ecuador to inform RSV immunoprophylaxis timing, given that acute bronchiolitis is mainly attributed to RSV and is the leading cause of infant hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease worldwide.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a national ecological time-series analysis of hospital discharges from the Ecuadorian Statistics Institute from 2007–2024, using data from 204 of 224 cantons with complete records, focusing on acute bronchiolitis (ICD-10 code J21) in children younger than 12 months (n = 23,190 nationally; 22,724 in the panel), with secondary outcomes across RSV-relevant age bands and RSV-specific ICD-10 codes.
analysis.methods: Analyses combined circular seasonality metrics with block-bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), year-by-year disaggregation, and complementary sensitivity analyses including the Moving Epidemics Method (MEM), Bai–Perron breaks, and lagged climate correlations, with K35 (appendicitis) as a negative control.
analysis.main_results: The weighted circular peak month of infant bronchiolitis hospitalizations shifted after the pandemic in Costa (+2.16 months), Sierra (+1.22), and Amazonía (+1.91), with attenuation by altitude; Costa was stable across 2022–2024, while Sierra and Amazonía showed year-to-year variability, and the composite RSV-coded outcome closely tracked ICD-10 code J21's timing in Costa and Sierra.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that bronchiolitis seasonality in Ecuador changed post-pandemic, with the most clear and stable changes in Costa, while Sierra showed a transient perturbation and Amazonía's estimates remained unstable and underpowered, highlighting the novelty of regional and altitudinal heterogeneity in RSV seasonality.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that a single national window for nirsevimab (February–April) and maternal RSVpreF (pregnancies expected to deliver January–May) is a more defensible starting point for immunoprophylaxis timing, given the varying stability of region-tailored estimates, pending confirmation from further seasons and laboratory-confirmed surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to limitations including year-to-year variability in Sierra and Amazonía, unstable estimates in Amazonía, and the pooled estimate requiring caution; the study's ecological design and reliance on ICD-10 codes as RSV proxies also present potential limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated regional, altitudinal, and age-specific heterogeneity of bronchiolitis hospitalization seasonality in Ecuador from 2007–2024 to inform RSV immunoprophylaxis timing. Using a national ecological time-series analysis of hospital discharges, the researchers found that the peak month of infant bronchiolitis hospitalizations shifted after the pandemic, with the most stable changes in Costa (+2.16 months), Sierra showing a transient perturbation (+1.22 months), and Amazonía exhibiting the most variability (+1.91 months). The composite RSV-coded outcome closely tracked ICD-10 code J21 in Costa and Sierra, supporting its use as a reasonable RSV proxy. The authors recommend a single national immunization window (nirsevimab February–April; maternal RSVpreF for pregnancies expected to deliver January–May) due to varying regional stability, with further surveillance needed for confirmation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决厄瓜多尔缺乏关于 毛细支气管炎 季节性、海拔模式和大流行后稳定性的地方证据的问题,以便为 RSV 免疫预防时机提供信息,因为急性 毛细支气管炎 主要归因于 RSV,并且是全球婴儿因下呼吸道疾病住院的主要原因。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对厄瓜多尔统计研究所 2007 年至 2024 年的出院情况进行了全国生态时间序列分析,使用了 224 个州中具有完整记录的 204 个州的数据,重点关注 12 个月以下儿童的急性 毛细支气管炎(ICD-10 代码 J21)(全国 n = 23,190 例;小组中的 22,724 例),次要结果涵盖RSV 相关年龄范围和 RSV 特定 ICD-10 代码。
elements_zh.methods: 分析将循环季节性指标与块引导置信区间 (CI)、逐年分解和补充敏感性分析相结合,包括移动流行病方法 (MEM)、Bai-Perron 断裂和滞后气候相关性,并以 K35(阑尾炎)作为阴性对照。
elements_zh.main_results: 科斯塔(+2.16 个月)、塞拉(+1.22)和亚马逊(+1.91)的婴儿 毛细支气管炎 住院加权循环高峰月发生了变化,并随海拔而衰减;科斯塔在 2022 年至 2024 年期间保持稳定,而塞拉利昂和亚马逊表现出逐年变化,复合 RSV 编码结果密切跟踪 ICD-10 代码 J21 在科斯塔和塞拉利昂的时间。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,厄瓜多尔的 毛细支气管炎 季节性在大流行后发生了变化,其中科斯塔的变化最为明显和稳定,而塞拉显示出短暂的扰动,而亚马逊的估计仍然不稳定且动力不足,突显了 RSV 季节性的区域和海拔异质性的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,鉴于各地区估计值的稳定性不同,有待进一步季节的确认和实验室确认的 监测,尼塞韦单抗(2 月至 4 月)和母亲 RSVpreF(预计于 1 月至 5 月分娩的妊娠)的单一国家窗口是免疫预防时机的更合理的起点。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于塞拉利昂和亚马逊地区的逐年变化、亚马逊地区的估计不稳定以及需要谨慎的汇总估计等限制,证据强度中等;该研究的生态设计和对 ICD-10 代码作为 RSV 代理的依赖也存在潜在的局限性。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,厄瓜多尔的 毛细支气管炎 季节性在大流行后发生了变化,其中科斯塔的变化最为明显和稳定,而塞拉显示出短暂的扰动,而亚马逊的估计仍然不稳定且动力不足,突显了 RSV 季节性的区域和海拔异质性的新颖性。

papers.title: SMAD4–BPIFA1 Axis Governs Airway Antiviral Defense in Myhre Syndrome
papers.abstract: Myhre syndrome is a rare autosomal-dominant disorder caused by gain-of-function (GOF) variants in SMAD4. Although it is primarily recognized as a fibrotic disease, we and others have identified respiratory infection-associated morbidity as a major clinical burden. Regardless, the epithelial-intrinsic mechanisms underlying increased viral susceptibility in Myhre syndrome remain poorly understood. Here, using patient-derived nasal airway epithelial cells (NECs) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection as a model, we demonstrate that infection is markedly exacerbated in Myhre syndrome epithelium relative to matched healthy controls. We further show that activation of TGF-β1–SMAD4 signaling in healthy donor NECs phenocopies augmented RSV susceptibility, identifying SMAD4 signaling as a bona fide pro-viral pathway in airway epithelium. Mechanistically, we identify a significant reduction in BPIFA1 expression in Myhre syndrome NECs. BPIFA1 is a key secreted innate defense protein with antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and emerging antiviral functions. SMAD signaling suppresses BPIFA1 expression, and its knockdown in healthy cells mimics the increased viral susceptibility, linking SMAD4 gain-of-function to impaired epithelial immunity. Therapeutically, we evaluated novel, stabilized 24-amino acid BPIFA1-derived peptides as a potential intervention. Treatment with active peptides (A4-153 and A4-X7) significantly reduced RSV infectivity and epithelial damage in both healthy and Myhre syndrome airway epithelial cultures, whereas a scrambled control peptide (A4-198) showed no significant effect. Collectively, our findings establish that GOF SMAD4 signaling enhances viral vulnerability in airway epithelium through suppression of BPIFA1-mediated antiviral defense and demonstrate that BPIFA1-derived peptide therapeutics represent a promising strategy to restore innate antiviral protection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Myhre syndrome, a rare autosomal-dominant disorder caused by gain-of-function SMAD4 variants, is primarily recognized as a fibrotic disease but carries significant respiratory infection-associated morbidity. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding epithelial-intrinsic mechanisms underlying increased viral susceptibility in Myhre syndrome.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used patient-derived nasal airway epithelial cells (NECs) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection as a model to compare Myhre syndrome epithelium with matched healthy controls. The research evaluated the role of TGF-β1–SMAD4 signaling and the antiviral protein BPIFA1 in airway epithelial susceptibility to RSV.
analysis.methods: The authors demonstrated RSV infection severity in Myhre syndrome NECs relative to healthy controls and showed that TGF-β1–SMAD4 activation in healthy donor NECs phenocopied augmented RSV susceptibility. Mechanistically, they linked SMAD4 gain-of-function to impaired epithelial immunity via suppression of BPIFA1 expression.
analysis.main_results: RSV infection was markedly exacerbated in Myhre syndrome epithelium compared to matched healthy controls. SMAD signaling suppressed BPIFA1 expression, and its knockdown in healthy cells increased viral susceptibility. Treatment with BPIFA1-derived peptides (A4-153 and A4-X7) significantly reduced RSV infectivity and epithelial damage, whereas a scrambled control peptide (A4-198) showed no significant effect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish that gain-of-function SMAD4 signaling enhances viral vulnerability in airway epithelium by suppressing BPIFA1-mediated antiviral defense. The study demonstrates that BPIFA1-derived peptide therapeutics represent a promising strategy to restore innate antiviral protection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that targeting the SMAD4–BPIFA1 axis could inform therapeutic strategies to mitigate RSV susceptibility in individuals with Myhre syndrome. The BPIFA1-derived peptides may offer a novel approach to enhance airway antiviral defense.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vitro models using patient-derived NECs and RSV as a model pathogen, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of in vivo validation and small sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates why individuals with Myhre syndrome, a rare genetic disorder caused by gain-of-function SMAD4 variants, exhibit increased susceptibility to respiratory infections. Using patient-derived nasal airway epithelial cells and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as a model, the authors demonstrate that RSV infection is markedly exacerbated in Myhre syndrome epithelium compared to healthy controls. Mechanistically, they show that SMAD4 signaling suppresses the expression of BPIFA1, a key secreted innate defense protein with antiviral functions, thereby impairing epithelial immunity. Therapeutically, stabilized BPIFA1-derived peptides (A4-153 and A4-X7) significantly reduced RSV infectivity and epithelial damage in both healthy and Myhre syndrome airway epithelial cultures, whereas a scrambled control peptide showed no effect. The findings establish a causal link between SMAD4 gain-of-function, BPIFA1 suppression, and heightened viral vulnerability, and suggest BPIFA1-derived peptides as a promising strategy to restore innate antiviral protection.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Myhre syndrome, a rare autosomal-dominant disorder caused by gain-of-function SMAD4 variants, is primarily recognized as a fibrotic disease but carries significant respiratory infection-associated morbidity. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding epithelial-intrinsic mechanisms underlying increased viral susceptibility in Myhre syndrome.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study used patient-derived nasal airway epithelial cells (NECs) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection as a model to compare Myhre syndrome epithelium with matched healthy controls. The research evaluated the role of TGF-β1–SMAD4 signaling and the antiviral protein BPIFA1 in airway epithelial susceptibility to RSV.
elements_en.methods: The authors demonstrated RSV infection severity in Myhre syndrome NECs relative to healthy controls and showed that TGF-β1–SMAD4 activation in healthy donor NECs phenocopied augmented RSV susceptibility. Mechanistically, they linked SMAD4 gain-of-function to impaired epithelial immunity via suppression of BPIFA1 expression.
elements_en.main_results: RSV infection was markedly exacerbated in Myhre syndrome epithelium compared to matched healthy controls. SMAD signaling suppressed BPIFA1 expression, and its knockdown in healthy cells increased viral susceptibility. Treatment with BPIFA1-derived peptides (A4-153 and A4-X7) significantly reduced RSV infectivity and epithelial damage, whereas a scrambled control peptide (A4-198) showed no significant effect.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish that gain-of-function SMAD4 signaling enhances viral vulnerability in airway epithelium by suppressing BPIFA1-mediated antiviral defense. The study demonstrates that BPIFA1-derived peptide therapeutics represent a promising strategy to restore innate antiviral protection.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that targeting the SMAD4–BPIFA1 axis could inform therapeutic strategies to mitigate RSV susceptibility in individuals with Myhre syndrome. The BPIFA1-derived peptides may offer a novel approach to enhance airway antiviral defense.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vitro models using patient-derived NECs and RSV as a model pathogen, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of in vivo validation and small sample size.

papers.title_zh: SMAD4–BPIFA1 轴控制气道 抗病毒药物 Myhre 综合征的防御
papers.source_body_en: Myhre syndrome is a rare autosomal-dominant disorder caused by gain-of-function (GOF) variants in SMAD4. Although it is primarily recognized as a fibrotic disease, we and others have identified respiratory infection-associated morbidity as a major clinical burden. Regardless, the epithelial-intrinsic mechanisms underlying increased viral susceptibility in Myhre syndrome remain poorly understood. Here, using patient-derived nasal airway epithelial cells (NECs) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection as a model, we demonstrate that infection is markedly exacerbated in Myhre syndrome epithelium relative to matched healthy controls. We further show that activation of TGF-β1–SMAD4 signaling in healthy donor NECs phenocopies augmented RSV susceptibility, identifying SMAD4 signaling as a bona fide pro-viral pathway in airway epithelium. Mechanistically, we identify a significant reduction in BPIFA1 expression in Myhre syndrome NECs. BPIFA1 is a key secreted innate defense protein with antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and emerging antiviral functions. SMAD signaling suppresses BPIFA1 expression, and its knockdown in healthy cells mimics the increased viral susceptibility, linking SMAD4 gain-of-function to impaired epithelial immunity. Therapeutically, we evaluated novel, stabilized 24-amino acid BPIFA1-derived peptides as a potential intervention. Treatment with active peptides (A4-153 and A4-X7) significantly reduced RSV infectivity and epithelial damage in both healthy and Myhre syndrome airway epithelial cultures, whereas a scrambled control peptide (A4-198) showed no significant effect. Collectively, our findings establish that GOF SMAD4 signaling enhances viral vulnerability in airway epithelium through suppression of BPIFA1-mediated antiviral defense and demonstrate that BPIFA1-derived peptide therapeutics represent a promising strategy to restore innate antiviral protection.

papers.title: Diagnostic performance and interchangeability of two commercial anti-RSV−IgG and IgA ELISAs across clinically relevant populations
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate assessment of anti-respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-specific antibodies has gained importance following the introduction of RSV vaccines and long-acting monoclonal antibody prophylaxis. However, the analytical performance and interchangeability of commercially available RSV−ELISAs remain insufficiently defined, leaving uncertainty about their reliability for clinical diagnostic practice. We performed a head-to-head comparison of the widely used commercial Euroimmun− and Virotech‒ELISA for detection of total anti-RSV‒IgG and IgA in 462 sera from four cohorts: healthy adults ( n = 100), pregnant women ( n = 59), children ( n = 101), and vaccinated transplant recipients ( n = 101; baseline and day + 30). Prefusion-F (pre-F)-specific IgG was quantified to infer functionally relevant antibody responses. Qualitative agreement, quantitative bias, correlations, and age-dependent patterns were assessed. Qualitative concordance in anti-RSV‒IgG detection was high (83.8%) between assays. However, the Virotech‒ELISA systematically yielded higher IgG detection rates and quantitative values ( P s = 0.92) and vaccinated transplant recipients (r s = 0.79). Anti-RSV‒IgA was detected infrequently (6%–11%), with moderate (79.4%) inter-assay concordance. IgG‒IgA correlations were weak in healthy adults and pregnant women (r s s ≥ 0.40). The Euroimmun− and Virotech‒ELISAs are not analytically interchangeable and exhibit systematic assay-dependent differences. Integrated analysis of total anti-RSV‒IgG, pre-F‒IgG, and IgA across clinically relevant populations emphasizes the need for assay- and population-aware interpretation to support reliable use of RSV serology in seroepidemiological studies and diagnostic laboratory practice. IMPORTANCE With the recent introduction of espiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines and infant monoclonal antibody prophylaxis, serological testing is gaining relevance in vaccine immunogenicity trials, post-licensure evaluations, and population-based serosurveillance. Although commercial ELISAs offer the potential to harmonize antibody testing, their appropriate application requires a detailed understanding of assay-specific performance and calibration characteristics. Inadequate validation can limit inter-laboratory comparability, such that identical samples yield different quantitative results across centers, thereby complicating longitudinal antibody monitoring and harmonized analysis in multicenter surveillance and vaccine studies. In this context, the present study provides a systematic cross-comparison of two widely used RSV−ELISAs and demonstrates that, despite good qualitative agreement, they are not quantitatively interchangeable and exhibit systematic differences in IgG and IgA measurements across populations and immune contexts. By characterizing the performance of total IgG, pre-F−specific IgG, and IgA in diverse clinical settings, this work supports informed assay selection and interpretation of RSV serology in clinical diagnostic practice.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 RBD fusion ameliorates enhanced disease induced by RSV G CCD mRNA vaccine in BALB/c mice
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a primary pathogen responsible for lower respiratory tract infections in both infants and the elderly. However, vaccine development has been consistently hampered by the risk of vaccine-enhanced disease (VED), while the role of the RSV attachment (G) glycoprotein has long been overlooked. Using an mRNA vaccine platform, this study systematically evaluated the roles of two critical RSV G protein domains—the central conserved domain (CCD) and the mucin-like domains—in mediating immune protection and VED. Results indicate that the mucin-like domains confer no protection and induce marked VED. Surprisingly, although CCD immunization elicits potent humoral immunity and significantly reduces viral load, it also induces Th2-biased responses and exacerbates pulmonary inflammation following RSV challenge. However, fusion of CCD with the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 in an mRNA vaccine (CCD + RBD) successfully redirected the Th2-biased immune responses toward a balanced Th1/Th2 profile, while significantly attenuating CCD-induced immunopathology. CD8+ T-cell depletion and adoptive-transfer experiments further supported a contribution of RBD-responsive CD8+ T cells to the reduction in pathology. These findings provide proof of concept that heterologous antigen fusion can reshape CCD-associated immunopathology in a BALB/c RSV challenge model.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a primary pathogen responsible for lower respiratory tract infections in both infants and the elderly, but vaccine development has been consistently hampered by the risk of vaccine-enhanced disease (VED), while the role of the RSV attachment (G) glycoprotein has long been overlooked.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using an mRNA vaccine platform, this study systematically evaluated the roles of two critical RSV G protein domains—the central conserved domain (CCD) and the mucin-like domains—in mediating immune protection and VED in BALB/c mice.
analysis.methods: The study employed mRNA vaccines targeting specific RSV G protein domains, including CCD and mucin-like domains, and evaluated immune responses and pathology following RSV challenge in BALB/c mice.
analysis.main_results: Results indicate that the mucin-like domains confer no protection and induce marked VED; CCD immunization elicits potent humoral immunity and significantly reduces viral load but also induces Th2-biased responses and exacerbates pulmonary inflammation following RSV challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that fusion of CCD with the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 in an mRNA vaccine (CCD + RBD) successfully redirected the Th2-biased immune responses toward a balanced Th1/Th2 profile while significantly attenuating CCD-induced immunopathology, providing proof of concept that heterologous antigen fusion can reshape CCD-associated immunopathology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that heterologous antigen fusion strategies could mitigate vaccine-enhanced disease risks for RSV vaccines, informing future vaccine design and development efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a BALB/c mouse model, which may limit generalizability to humans; however, the evidence strength is high due to the systematic evaluation of specific domains and the use of controlled experiments.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of RSV G protein domains in vaccine-enhanced disease (VED) using an mRNA vaccine platform in BALB/c mice. The mucin-like domains conferred no protection and induced marked VED, while CCD elicited potent immunity but also Th2-biased responses and pulmonary inflammation. Fusion of CCD with SARS-CoV-2 RBD redirected responses to a balanced Th1/Th2 profile and attenuated immunopathology, supported by CD8+ T-cell experiments. These findings demonstrate that heterologous antigen fusion can mitigate VED risks, informing future RSV vaccine design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是导致婴儿和老年人下呼吸道感染的主要病原体,但 疫苗 的发展一直受到 疫苗 增强疾病 (VED) 风险的阻碍,而 RSV 附着 (G) 糖蛋白的作用长期以来一直被忽视。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用 mRNA 疫苗 平台,系统评估了两个关键 RSV G 蛋白结构域(中央保守结构域 (CCD) 和粘蛋白样结构域)在介导 BALB/c 小鼠免疫保护和 VED 中的作用。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用针对特定 RSV G 蛋白结构域(包括 CCD 和粘蛋白样结构域)的 mRNA 疫苗,并评估了 BALB/c 小鼠 RSV 攻击后的 免疫应答 和病理学。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,粘蛋白样结构域不提供保护并诱导显着的 VED;CCD 免疫引发有效的体液免疫并显着降低病毒载量,但也会诱导 Th2 偏向反应并加剧 RSV 攻击后的肺部炎症。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,CCD 与 SARS-CoV-2 的受体结合域 (RBD) 在 mRNA 疫苗 (CCD + RBD) 中的融合成功地将 Th2 偏向的 免疫应答 重定向到平衡的 Th1/Th2 谱,同时显着减弱 CCD 诱导的免疫病理学,这提供了异源抗原融合可以重塑 CCD 相关免疫病理学的概念证明。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,异源抗原融合策略可以减轻 疫苗 增强的 RSV 疫苗 疾病风险,为未来的 疫苗 设计和开发工作提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在 BALB/c 小鼠模型中进行的,这可能限制了对人类的推广;然而,由于对特定领域的系统评估和对照实验的使用,证据强度很高。

papers.title: Benchmarking and optimisation of bait-capture metagenomics for sequencing of respiratory viruses at scale
papers.abstract: Sequencing respiratory virus genomes is essential for public health surveillance and research. Although shotgun metagenomics is pathogen agnostic, its sensitivity is limited by abundant off-target host nucleic acids. Hybridization bait capture overcomes this limitation by selectively enriching viral sequences prior to sequencing. We evaluated three respiratory viral bait capture workflows (veSEQ, RVI-seq, and Illumina) to compare their performance and assess their suitability for scalable respiratory virus sequencing. Synthetic RNA controls and clinical samples containing SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, human parainfluenza virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were analysed. All three workflows demonstrated high efficiency, reproducibility and broadly comparable performance across respiratory viruses. Complete viral genomes were consistently recovered from samples containing 10,000 viral copies, while viral reads remained detectable at substantially lower viral loads, including approximately 100 copies. Workflow optimisation reduced reagent costs and enabled laboratory automation without compromising sequencing sensitivity. Hybridization bait capture provides an effective and scalable approach for respiratory virus genome sequencing. Cost reductions and automation can be implemented without compromising performance, supporting its use in routine genomic surveillance and public health preparedness.

source_records.title: Benchmarking and optimisation of bait-capture metagenomics for sequencing of respiratory viruses at scale
source_records.abstract: Abstract Sequencing of respiratory virus genomes is important for public health and research. Shotgun metagenomics although pathogen agnostic is limited by off-target DNA/RNA. Bait capture metagenomics (hybridization capture) overcomes this by selectively enriching a targeted component of the library. We sought to evaluate three different respiratory virus bait capture methods to determine any advantages between methods. We show that all three bait capture methods demonstrated high efficiency and reproducibility and generated broadly comparable results, with some minor variation at low viral copy numbers. We show that further optimisations to reduce costs and to enable automation are possible without impacting sensitivity. Overall, we demonstrate that viral bait capture methods are broadly effective for respiratory viruses and that cost reductions can be achieved without compromising performance. These results provide confidence in viral bait capture methods for the routine global surveillance of respiratory viruses for global public health monitoring and preparedness.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 对呼吸道病毒 基因组 进行测序对于公共卫生和研究至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了三种呼吸道病毒诱饵捕获工作流程(veSEQ、RVI-seq 和 Illumina),以比较它们的性能并评估它们对可扩展呼吸道病毒测序的适用性。
elements_zh.methods: 杂交诱饵捕获通过在测序前选择性富集病毒序列来克服这一限制。对含有 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、人副流感病毒和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的合成 RNA 对照和临床样本进行了分析。工作流程优化降低了试剂成本并实现了实验室自动化,同时又不影响测序灵敏度。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有三个工作流程在呼吸道病毒中都表现出高效率、可重复性和广泛可比的性能。完整的病毒 基因组 始终从含有 10,000 个病毒拷贝的样本中回收,而病毒读数在病毒载量大幅降低(包括大约 100 个拷贝)的情况下仍然可检测到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 杂交诱饵捕获为呼吸道病毒 基因组 测序提供了一种有效且可扩展的方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 可以在不影响性能的情况下实现成本降低和自动化,支持其在常规 基因组监测 和公共卫生准备中的使用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管鸟枪法宏基因组学与病原体无关,但其敏感性受到大量脱靶 宿主 核酸的限制。由于对多个工作流程的综合评估以及跨病毒载量的一致结果,证据强度很高。

papers.title: RSV shapes serotype-specific invasive pneumococcal disease dynamics in children: an observational study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pneumococcal nasopharyngeal colonization is the first step toward invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) may trigger IPD, particularly for serotypes with low disease potential. We aimed to analyse the distribution of pneumococcal serotypes among paediatric IPD according to RSV circulation level. Methods We used data from three continuous French surveillance systems on IPD, pneumococcal carriage and RSV infections from 2008 to 2023. Based on the RSV epidemics threshold, we assessed the proportion of each serotype among IPD, depending on “RSV season” and “non-RSV season”. We assessed the correlation between the likelihood of serotype-specific involvement in IPD according to non-RSV season vs RSV season and the estimated disease potential of each serotype. Results Among 4,574 IPD cases, the serotype distribution strongly varied during non-RSV season vs RSV season. The lower the disease potential of serotypes, the more RSV circulation enhanced their involvement in IPD (Rho=0.60, CI95% 0.28 to 0.80, p-value = 0.0012). Conclusions The role of RSV in triggering IPD strongly varies across pneumococcal serotypes. The impact of RSV-targeted interventions should be evaluated in light of these data.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,RSV 在引发 IPD 中的作用在不同肺炎球菌血清型中存在很大差异,这凸显了之前未被充分认识的血清型特异性相互作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对 RSV 的干预措施可能需要考虑 IPD 风险中血清型特异性动态,为未来的 疫苗接种 和 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其观察设计和对 监测 数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差并限制因果推断。由于缺乏实验对照和潜在的未测量的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

Britannica Editors Last updated Aug. 1, 2026 •History Britannica AI Ask Anything Table of Contents Table of Contents Ask Anything respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), infectious agent of the respiratory system that typically produces a mild coldlike illness but in susceptible individuals, particularly infants under six months of age, is a major cause of severe and potentially fatal lower respiratory disease. Severe bronchiolitis and pneumonia caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) occurs most commonly in the elderly and in young children. An estimated 60 to 70 percent of children have been infected with RSV by age one, and nearly all children have been infected by age two. Because RSV effectively evades immunity, repeat infections are common. RSV infection is seasonal, occurring as an annual epidemic during the winter in most countries in temperate regions. What's the Difference Between Bacteria and Viruses?Knowing the difference isn't just a technical distinction—it can save lives.(more) See all videos for this article Direct person-to-person contact is thought to be the most common route of RSV transmission. The virus also can be transmitted through the air, such as by coughing or sneezing, and through direct contact with a contaminated surface followed by touching of the face. Symptoms generally appear within four to six days of infection and include runny nose, cough, sore throat, headache, fever, and wheezing. In instances of severe illness, affected individuals may have a high fever, severe wheezing, rapid or laboured breathing, and bluish lips or fingers. Infants may only show signs of irritability, fatigue, and breathing difficulties, even in severe cases. Related Topics: pneumonia bronchiolitis ribavirin respiratory syncytial virus infection Pneumovirus (Show more) On the Web: National Center for Biotechnology Information - Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Children (Aug. 01, 2026) (Show more) See all related content The only pharmacological therapy available for treatment of RSV is the nucleoside analogue ribavirin, which can be administered orally, parenterally (by injection or infusion), or by inhalation. An injectable humanized monoclonal antibody is available for prevention of severe RSV illness in high-risk infants and children. It provides passive immunity and must by given by intramuscular injection once a month during RSV season. Transmission can be prevented with frequent handwashing, cleaning of surfaces, avoiding close contact with others, and covering the mouth and nose with the upper arm when coughing or sneezing. analysis.brief_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common infectious agent causing mild coldlike illness but severe lower respiratory disease in vulnerable populations, particularly infants under six months, young children, and the elderly. It is highly contagious, with 60-70% of children infected by age one and nearly all by age two. RSV spreads through direct contact, airborne transmission, and contaminated surfaces, with symptoms ranging from runny nose and fever to severe wheezing and breathing difficulties. The virus is seasonal, peaking in winter in temperate regions. Treatment options are limited, with ribavirin as the primary pharmacological therapy, and a monoclonal antibody available for prevention in high-risk infants. Prevention emphasizes hygiene and avoiding close contact during outbreaks.

news.content_title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) News, Articles and Research
news.content: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Nirsevimab is a long-acting monoclonal antibody that provides season-long protection against RSV in infants, reducing medically attended infections and hospitalizations. Maternal vaccination and nirsevimab together offer complementary strategies to protect newborns during their highest-risk months. Overview Feature Articles Latest Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) News and Research Early-infancy infection with RSV increases the risk of developing childhood asthma Belgian scientists from VIB and Ghent University (UGent), together with Danish collaborators, have uncovered compelling evidence that early-infancy infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) significantly increases the risk of developing childhood asthma-especially in children with a family history of allergy or asthma. Year-round access to RSV immunization may reduce major seasonal outbreaks Providing year-round access to RSV immunization would minimize the risk of large seasonal outbreaks across the nation, including in both urban and rural areas. Preparing for the respiratory virus season: A guide for families As respiratory virus season begins, pediatric experts are preparing for an expected rise in cases of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), which can cause cold-like symptoms in most people but serious illness in infants and older adults. COVID-19, RSV, and flu vaccines remain safe and effective The systematic review provides crucial insights into the efficacy and safety of respiratory virus vaccines, supporting evidence-based immunization practices. Study reveals impact of viral combinations on infant respiratory illness severity A new study led by researchers at National Jewish Health has revealed that, while a wide range of viruses can cause lower respiratory tract illnesses (LRIs) in infants, certain viruses and viral combinations dramatically increase the risk of severe disease. A parent's guide to manage pediatric respiratory illnesses during the virus season As we head deeper into fall and toward the holiday season, your little one may start to exhibit symptoms like a runny nose, cough, or fever. elements_zh.event: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是五岁以下儿童急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因,对全世界儿童健康构成持续威胁。婴儿早期感染 RSV 会显着增加患儿童哮喘的风险,尤其是有过敏或哮喘家族史的儿童。RSV 还会导致老年人出现严重后果和心脏并发症。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: RSV 导致成人住院率较高,丹麦的一项大型真实世界随机试验发现,RSVpreF 疫苗 将 60 岁及以上成人与 RSV 相关的住院率降低了 80% 以上。单剂量的 RSV 疫苗 可以为老年人提供 58% 的住院保护,但对于免疫功能低下的个体来说,效果有所不同。全年接种 RSV 疫苗可能会减少全国主要季节性 暴发 的发生。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 儿科专家正在为呼吸道病毒季节期间 RSV 病例的预期增加做好准备。孕产妇 疫苗接种 和 尼塞韦单抗 共同提供补充策略,在新生儿风险最高的月份提供保护。世界卫生组织 (WHO) 发布了第一份关于保护婴儿免受 RSV 感染的免疫产品的立场文件。然而,HEPA 净化器并不能完全减少教室病毒暴露,这表明需要采取额外的干预措施。

news.content: Deadline: 10-Sep-2026 Pfizer Global Medical Grants (GMG), in collaboration with the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM), has launched a Quality Improvement Grant opportunity to improve maternal RSV immunization delivery during pregnancy across healthcare systems in the United States. The grant supports evidence-based quality improvement projects that increase vaccine access, reduce barriers, improve healthcare workflows, and strengthen maternal and infant health outcomes. Overview of Pfizer Global Medical Grants Maternal RSV Immunization Quality Improvement Grant Pfizer Global Medical Grants (GMG), together with the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM), is supporting independent quality improvement initiatives focused on improving the delivery of maternal Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) immunization during pregnancy. The grant opportunity aims to strengthen healthcare systems by supporting projects that improve how maternal RSV vaccination is delivered, accessed, and adopted in real-world clinical settings. The program focuses on applying existing evidence and best practices to improve vaccination processes rather than conducting clinical research or testing vaccine effectiveness. The initiative encourages healthcare organizations, providers, and community partners to develop scalable models that improve: - Maternal RSV immunization uptake. - Vaccine access. - Healthcare workflow integration. - Patient-provider communication. - Equity in maternal healthcare. - Long-term sustainability of immunization programs. Purpose of the Grant Program The primary goal of this Quality Improvement Grant is to support healthcare systems in improving maternal RSV immunization during pregnancy through practical and sustainable improvements. The program seeks to address challenges such as: - Limited awareness about maternal RSV immunization. - Healthcare workflow barriers. - Communication gaps between providers and patients. - Vaccine access challenges. - Health disparities affecting underserved communities. - Lack of coordination between maternal and pediatric healthcare services. Funded projects should focus on improving healthcare delivery systems and creating measurable improvements in vaccination outcomes. What Is Maternal RSV Immunization? Maternal RSV immunization refers to vaccination provided during pregnancy to help protect newborn infants from Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infection. RSV is a common respiratory virus that can cause serious illness, especially in infants and young children. Improving maternal RSV immunization delivery can help: - Increase protection for newborns. - Reduce severe RSV-related illness. - Improve preventive healthcare practices. - Strengthen coordination between maternal and infant care providers. Key Focus Areas of the Grant The grant supports projects that improve maternal RSV immunization through system-level interventions and healthcare improvements. Priority areas include: Improving Healthcare Workflow Integration Projects may focus on integrating RSV immunization into routine maternal healthcare services. Examples include: - Adding vaccination processes into prenatal care workflows. - Improving electronic health record reminders. - Creating standardized vaccination protocols. - Reducing missed vaccination opportunities. Strengthening Care Coordination The program encourages collaboration between healthcare professionals involved in maternal and infant care. Potential partners include: - Maternal-fetal medicine specialists. - Obstetricians. - Nurses. - Midwives. - Doulas. - Pediatricians. - Family medicine providers. - Pharmacists. - Public health organizations. - Community organizations. Improving Provider and Patient Communication Projects may develop strategies to improve understanding and acceptance of maternal RSV vaccination. Activities may include: - Provider education. - Patient communication tools. - Vaccine counseling approaches. - Awareness initiatives. Reducing Barriers to Vaccine Uptake The grant supports initiatives that address structural and behavioral barriers, including: - Limited healthcare access. - Vaccine hesitancy. - Transportation challenges. - Healthcare inequalities. - Information gaps. Increasing Health Equity Priority is given to projects that improve vaccination access among: - Underserved communities. - Rural populations. - Maternal care deserts. - Communities experiencing healthcare disparities. Why This Grant Opportunity Matters Maternal RSV immunization plays an important role in protecting infants from serious respiratory illness. However, healthcare systems may face challenges in ensuring that eligible pregnant individuals receive recommended vaccinations. This grant supports improvements that can help healthcare organizations: - Increase vaccine coverage. - Improve maternal and infant health outcomes. - Create sustainable immunization systems. - Reduce healthcare disparities. - Develop scalable quality improvement models. By focusing on system-level improvements, the program aims to create lasting changes in maternal healthcare delivery. Funding Information The Pfizer Global Medical Grants Quality Improvement Grant provides financial support for eligible quality improvement initiatives. Available Funding - Single-site or regional projects: Up to USD 100,000 - Large multi-site projects: Up to USD 200,000 Estimated Total Funding Available - Approximately USD 200,000 Funding amounts may vary depending on project scope, impact, and available resources. Project Timeline Funded projects are expected to follow the proposed implementation schedule. Key timeline details include: - Expected project start date: December 2026 - Project period: Through the 2027–2028 RSV and respiratory disease season - Maximum project duration: 18 months Projects should demonstrate measurable progress and outcomes during the funding period. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The opportunity is open to organizations in the United States proposing independent quality improvement initiatives. Eligible applicants should: - Be involved in healthcare delivery or improvement activities. - Have the ability to implement maternal RSV immunization improvement projects. - Demonstrate organizational capacity. - Develop measurable quality improvement goals. Applicants may include healthcare organizations, healthcare systems, and collaborative groups working to improve maternal healthcare delivery. Eligible Project Characteristics Strong applications should include: - Evidence-based quality improvement strategies. - Clear implementation plans. - Measurable outcomes. - Sustainable healthcare system improvements. - Multidisciplinary collaboration. - Defined roles for participating organizations. Projects should focus on improving current healthcare practices rather than conducting clinical research. How to Apply for the Pfizer Maternal RSV Immunization Grant Applicants must submit applications through the designated online application portal. A complete application should include: Project Proposal Applicants should describe: - Project objectives. - Current challenges. - Proposed quality improvement strategies. - Expected impact. - Implementation approach. Project Timeline Applications should provide: - Key project activities. - Implementation milestones. - Expected completion dates. - Evaluation periods. Organizational Information Applicants must provide details about: - Organization background. - Relevant healthcare experience. - Project leadership team. - Partner organizations. Budget Information Applicants must submit: - Detailed project budget. - Requested funding amount. - Budget justification. - Costs in U.S. dollars. Supporting Documentation Applications should include required supporting documents listed in the official request for proposals. Allowable and Non-Allowable Expenses Funding may support project implementation activities. Allowable Expenses Grant funds may support: - Quality improvement activities. - Project implementation. - Program coordination. - Equipment hire or leasing when appropriate. - Other approved project-related expenses. Non-Allowable Expenses Funding cannot be used for: - Capital purchases. - Purchase of Pfizer therapeutic products. - Activities unrelated to quality improvement objectives. Institutional overhead is allowed according to Pfizer’s maximum allowable rate. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No cases, deaths, or exposures are reported; the event is a regulatory approval, not an outbreak. No risk level is stated.

analysis.brief_en: Shiyang Group (01093.HK) has secured approval from China’s National Medical Products Administration to launch clinical trials for its recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, SYS6057. The announcement, made on July 31, 2026, confirms that the vaccine has met regulatory requirements and can now be tested in human subjects within China. No outbreak data—such as cases, deaths, or exposures—are associated with this event; it represents a development milestone rather than a public health emergency. The approval enables the company to proceed with phase I/II studies, potentially accelerating the availability of an RSV prevention option for the Chinese population. No additional public health measures or risk assessments are required at this stage beyond the standard clinical trial oversight.

No additional public health measures or risk assessments are required at this stage beyond the standard clinical trial oversight.

news.content_zh: 石羊集团(01093.HK)重组呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疫苗、SYS6057已获得国家药品监督管理局批准开展临床试验。该公告于 2026 年 7 月 31 日发布,确认 疫苗 已满足监管要求,现在可以在中国境内进行人体受试者测试。没有 暴发 数据(例如病例、死亡或暴露)与此事件相关;它代表着一个发展里程碑,而不是公共卫生紧急事件。该批准使该公司能够继续进行 I/II 期研究,有可能加速为中国人群提供 RSV 预防方案。除标准临床试验监督外,现阶段不需要采取额外的公共卫生措施或风险评估。

Conditions Pregnant Patients Caught Between Two Vaccine Schedules Now Have Infant Hospitalization Numbers to Bring to the Appointment Published Jul 31, 2026 3:15 PM EDT By Dorothy Brooks NORBERTO DUARTE | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Pregnant patients in the United States are now navigating something that did not exist a year ago: two credible immunization schedules that do not match. And for the first time, they have hard numbers on infant hospitalizations to bring into that conversation. Researchers at the University of Pittsburgh and UPMC reported in JAMA Network Open on June 5 that among infants younger than three months, maternal RSV vaccination was associated with roughly 68 percent effectiveness against hospitalization for RSV-related respiratory illness and about 69 percent effectiveness against more severe lower respiratory tract disease. That finding lands in the middle of a guidance split. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists released its own 2026 maternal immunization schedule in June, the first time the organization has published recommendations separate from federal ones. The schedule was endorsed by 13 medical and health organizations, including the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Diseases Society of America, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, and it followed ACOG's withdrawal from the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices in February 2026. For an expectant parent, this is not an abstract governance dispute. It is the reason two clinicians can give different answers in the same week, and the reason a pharmacy and an obstetric practice may operate from different documents. Numbers Parents Can Actually Use The Pittsburgh study was built around a question families actually ask. It examined infants 90 days old or younger who were hospitalized for respiratory illness in western Pennsylvania across the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 RSV seasons, comparing outcomes between those whose mothers received the RSVpreF vaccine during pregnancy and those whose mothers did not. Infants who received the separate monoclonal antibody after birth were excluded so the two approaches would not be confused. "We designed this study to focus on what matters most to families," said lead author Anne-Marie Rick, MD, PhD, of Pitt School of Medicine and UPMC, in a UPMC statement. The scale of the underlying problem gives those percentages meaning. RSV is the leading cause of infant hospitalization in the United States, and CDC figures cited by the research team indicate roughly two to three of every 100 babies younger than three months are hospitalized each year because of it. Severe cases can require oxygen support or mechanical ventilation. A separate and larger analysis published in JAMA Pediatrics in March 2026, drawn from a seven-site CDC surveillance network, estimated that both the maternal RSV vaccine and the infant monoclonal antibody protected infants against RSV-associated hospitalization during the 2024-2025 season. That study was not industry-funded and reached a consistent conclusion, which strengthens the overall picture. Two Schedules, One Appointment The ACOG schedule lists four routinely recommended maternal vaccines: inactivated or recombinant influenza vaccine at any trimester, COVID-19 vaccine, Tdap preferably during weeks 27 through 36 of each pregnancy, and the maternal RSV vaccine between 32 weeks 0 days and 36 weeks 6 days of gestation. The clearest point of divergence is COVID-19. ACOG continues to recommend COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy; current CDC guidance does not carry the same recommendation. ACOG also specifies that the live attenuated intranasal influenza vaccine is not indicated during pregnancy, though it is acceptable after delivery. ACOG has stated its position plainly. "It is well documented that respiratory conditions can cause poor outcomes during pregnancy," ACOG President Steven J. Fleischman, MD, MBA, said in an organizational statement. On RSV specifically, the two approaches are complementary rather than competing. Clinical guidance holds that an infant generally needs one form of protection, not both. If the mother received the vaccine at least 14 days before delivery, the infant typically does not need the monoclonal antibody. If she was not vaccinated, or delivered within 14 days of vaccination, the infant should receive the antibody after birth during RSV season. Timing is also seasonal. In most of the continental United States, the maternal RSV vaccine is given between September and January, which means patients due this fall are making the decision right now. Jurisdictions with different seasonality, including Alaska and some tropical territories, follow local guidance. Reading the Study's Limits Alongside Its Findings The funding and design details belong next to the headline number, not buried below it. The JAMA Network Open study was funded by Pfizer Inc through a collaboration with the University of Pittsburgh, and Pfizer employees are among the co-authors. Rick reported receiving grant support from Pfizer during the study and personal fees plus a site principal investigator role for a Pfizer vaccine trial outside the submitted work. Several other Pitt and UPMC co-authors reported Pfizer grant support. Pfizer manufactures the RSVpreF vaccine that the study evaluated. Beyond funding, the design carries real constraints. This was a retrospective case-control analysis using a test-negative design within a single health system in one region, not a randomized trial. Effectiveness estimates from one health system and one geography may not transfer cleanly to populations with different demographics, care patterns, or RSV circulation. The analysis covered infants 90 days or younger, so it does not speak to protection later in the first year. The research team acknowledged those limits and is continuing the work. The study is part of an ongoing four-year effort that will follow the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 seasons and extend the analysis to infants up to 180 days old, which should address how long protection lasts. Preparing for the Obstetrician Conversation The purpose of this data is to make the appointment more productive, not to settle the decision in advance. Vaccination during pregnancy is a personal medical decision that belongs with a qualified clinician who knows the individual history. Patients can reasonably ask which schedule their practice is following and why, since the answer determines what they will be offered. They can ask about timing, particularly whether their due date and the 32 to 36 week RSV window line up, and what happens if delivery comes early. They can ask whether the infant monoclonal antibody is the better route in their situation, and confirm the 14-day threshold that determines which product the baby needs. Insurance is worth raising directly. When professional society recommendations diverge from federal ones, coverage can follow the federal schedule, and patients should confirm with their plan rather than assume. Patients covered by Medicaid or receiving care at a federally qualified health center should ask what is stocked on site, since availability varies by practice and pharmacy. Considerable uncertainty remains. Whether federal guidance will shift again, how insurers will handle the divergence through the coming respiratory season, and how long maternal antibody protection persists in infants are all unresolved. Updated CDC respiratory season guidance and the next round of surveillance data are expected before the fall season begins. MedicalDaily will track both. news.content_title: NHS confirms major vaccine rollout for older adults from September
news.content: Claire Schofield Updated Tue, 4 August 2026 at 1:04 pm UTC 0 Adults aged between 65 and 74 years in certain clinical at risk groups are to be offered the RSV jab (Image: Getty) NHS England and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) have confirmed a major vaccine rollout for older adults from September. The NHS Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) vaccination programme is being expanded to adults aged between 65 and 74 years in certain clinical at risk groups this year. The RSV vaccine has been routinely available to older adults as they turn 75 since September 2024, and was later extended to include all adults aged 80 and over, and all residents in care homes in April 2026. But NHS has confirmed a further expansion from next month with the eligibility criteria to include adults aged 65 to 74 years following advice from the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI). NHS England and the UKHSA confirmed the change last month and said GPs will offer the vaccine to those who are eligible from September 1. RSV is a common cause of coughs and colds and while it usually gets better by itself, it can cause severe illness for babies and older adults over the age of 75. Those who are infected with RSV typically experience cold-like symptoms including a runny or blocked nose, a cough, sneezing, tiredness and a high temperature, but it can also lead to more serious infections like pneumonia or bronchiolitis. The RSV vaccination is available on the NHS for free to eligible groups, which can help reduce the risk of becoming seriously ill from the infection. You can currently get the jab if: you're 28 weeks pregnant or more you're aged 75 or over you live in a care home for older adults But from September 1, 2026, adults aged 65 to 74 and in either of the following clinical at risk groups will become eligible to get the RSV vaccine: 1. Chronic respiratory disease including those with: poorly controlled asthma chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and emphysema bronchiectasis cystic fibrosis interstitial lung fibrosis pneumoconiosis bronchopulmonary dysplasia 2. Immunosuppression due to disease or treatment. Confirming the expansion in a letter on July 1, Caroline Temmink, director of vaccination at NHS England, and Dr Mary Ramsay CBE, director of public health programmes (including immunisation) at the UKHSA, said: "From 1 September 2026, the eligibility criteria will be expanded further to include adults aged 65 to 74 years in certain clinical at risk groups as advised by the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI): chronic respiratory disease immunosuppression due to disease or treatment "Key points about the changes to the programme: the vaccine used in the programme will continue to be Abrysvo® (Pfizer pre-F vaccine) on a one-dose schedule. Adults who receive the vaccine from 1 September 2026 because they are aged 65 to 74 years old and in a clinical risk group should not be invited for a further dose of Abrysvo® when they become 75 years old RSV vaccines can be administered at any time and offers of vaccination should continue throughout the year. RSV vaccination should not be routinely scheduled with influenza vaccination but can be co-administered with the COVID-19 vaccine GP providers are expected to deliver a 100% offer to eligible groups, with call and recall delivered at the earliest opportunity where community pharmacies have been commissioned to support the older adults RSV programme, an updated enhanced service specification will be issued ahead of 1 September, and commissioned community pharmacies will be invited by regions to enter a contract variation."
